intent: Which watering rules apply to a Louviers yard, what each drought stage allows while a yard is being redone, and what else local (new water lines, the water supply, the soil) should shape a turf layout?
distinctValue: Louviers has its own water and sanitation district with its own signed drought restrictions, adopted 21 April 2026: homes water Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday at Stage 1 (never 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.), Tuesday and Saturday at Stage 2, when no new lawns, trees, perennials or shrubs may be planted, and Stage 3 may prohibit all outdoor use. None of the nearest pages (Sterling Ranch, Highlands Ranch, Castle Pines, Castle Rock) has these days, the Stage 2 planting ban, the district's penalty ladder or its written-notice rule. The page also carries the district's 2026 water main and service line replacement (a reason to locate lines before a base is dug), the variance process and its September/October/November 2026 board meetings, and USDA soil data showing mostly well-drained ground at and around the center of town, with one small pocket of high-clay Louviers soil on nearby slopes. The district's site does not say which stage is in force as of 12 September 2026, so the page tells the reader to find the notice or ask.

sources.label: Louviers Water and Sanitation District: resolution adopting drought and water shortage restrictions (signed)
supports: "APPROVED AND ADOPTED THIS 21st day of April 2026."
"The District owns, operates, and maintains water facilities and improvements, including a water supply, storage, treatment, and distribution system"
"At the sole discretion of the Board, Drought and Water Shortage Restrictions (the “Restrictions”) will go into effect for limited periods of time."
"The following Restrictions apply to all customers and users of the Louviers Water and Sanitation District (the “District”) and pertain to the use of water supplied by the District."
"There are four stages of Restrictions (each a “Stage”): a. Voluntary Drought Restrictions b. Stage 1 Drought Restrictions c. Stage 2 Drought Restrictions d. Stage 3 Drought Restrictions"

"The District will provide written notice to all customers when a Stage is implemented. This notice shall specify: a. The specific stage in effect; b. The effective date of the stage; and c. The restrictions that customers are required to follow during the designated stage."

Penalties: "Upon a first violation, the District will issue a written notice to the customer identifying the violation." / Second: "inform the customer that a Violation Charge will be applied to the customer’s water bill." / Third: "The notice will also advise the customer of the opportunity for a hearing" / Fourth: "the District may temporarily discontinue the customer’s water service until the violation is corrected and all outstanding penalties and water service charges have been paid ... The customer will be responsible for all applicable service shut off/turn on fees."
Voluntary: "All Stage 1 Drought Restrictions on a voluntary basis. No enforcement, and no penalties or fines for noncompliance."

Stage 1: "All customers shall limit outdoor watering to no more than three days per week." / "Residential property: Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday." / "All other Property (including DuPont Park, Triangle Park, Village Club Park and right-of-way taps): Monday, Wednesday, and Friday." / "Outdoor watering is prohibited between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m."

Stage 1: "Trees, shrubs, and perennials may be watered on any day using a hand-held hose or other low-volume, dripline, or non-spray irrigation methods." / "Annuals plantings, vegetable/fruit/herb gardens and community gardens ... may be watered on any day using a hand-held hose or other low-volume, dripline, or non-spray irrigation methods."
Stage 1: "Power washing is only permitted on assigned watering days, except when necessary for immediate health or safety reasons."

Stages 1 and 2: "The Board may, in its discretion, grant variances from these restrictions. Variances may be approved in writing for specific uses, water sources, time periods, seasonal needs, or other circumstances as determined by the Board."

Stage 2: "All customers shall limit outdoor watering to no more than two days per week." / "Residential property: Tuesday and Saturday." / "Outdoor watering is prohibited between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m."

Stage 2: "Existing trees, shrubs, and perennials should be watered in accordance with the Outdoor Irrigation Schedule and only by means of a hand-held hose or other low-volume, dripline, or non-spray irrigation methods. No new lawns, trees, perennials, or shrubs may be planted."
Stage 2: "No new annual plantings, vegetable/fruit/herb gardens and community gardens may be planted."
Stage 2: "The use of water to clean outdoor impervious surfaces such as sidewalks, driveways and patios is prohibited, except when necessary for immediate public health or safety reasons."
Stage 3: "A Stage 3 response activates a rationing program. ... During this stage, all outdoor water use may be prohibited, and indoor water use may be restricted."
The document does not mention artificial, synthetic or nonvegetative turf.
